key_insight: VGGT-Ω shows that feed-forward 3D reconstruction models scale predictably with model and data size, and by scaling and architectural improvements it delivers substantially better accuracy, efficiency, and support for both static and dynamic scenes.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between optimization-based reconstructors and fast feed-forward models by improving reconstruction quality and runtime while preserving geometry-aware features useful for downstream tasks.
method: Design and scale up a new feed-forward reconstructor (VGGT-Ω) with architecture and training modifications to improve capacity and efficiency.
Train at much larger model and data scale, empirically demonstrating predictable scaling behavior (performance vs. model/data size).
Preserve and enhance geometry-aware feature representations to support accurate reconstructions for static and dynamic scenes and enable downstream uses.
impact: Enables practitioners to get near-optimization-level reconstruction quality with orders-of-magnitude faster inference and better support for dynamic scenes, making large-scale, real-time 3D pipelines more practical.
visual_elements: Log–log scaling plot: reconstruction error vs. model/data size showing predictable improvement curves.
Before/after qualitative comparison: side-by-side renderings of static and dynamic scene reconstructions (baseline vs. VGGT-Ω).
Architecture diagram: high-level blocks highlighting key changes that enable scaling and geometry-aware features.
Efficiency chart: latency/throughput and accuracy trade-off bars comparing VGGT-Ω to optimization-based and prior feed-forward models.
paper_authors: Jianyuan Wang, Minghao Chen, Shangzhan Zhang, Nikita Karaev, Johannes Schönberger
